children: The near-term outlook for Malaysian banks appears more cautious amid elevated funding costs and emerging asset-quality risks, Affin Hwang IB analyst Chin Jin Han says in a note. Banks are expected to tighten asset-quality management to contain risks in retail and selected business loans, he says. However, stronger wealth-management and fee income, alongside net interest income-driven focus, should help offset weaker net interest margin and trading conditions, he reckons. Capital management and attractive dividend yields are also expected to provide support, he adds. Affin Hwang maintains an overweight rating on Malaysian banking sector, pegging AMMB and Public Bank as top picks. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
